Cao Yu is a leading Chinese cinematographer known for visually distinctive, large‑scale feature films and for long‑running collaborations with major mainland directors, especially Lu Chuan and Guan Hu. He is also widely known in Chinese popular culture as the husband of actress Yao Chen.

Career highlights and style
- Training: Graduated from the Cinematography Department of the Beijing Film Academy (BFA). He began with shorts, commercials, and music videos before moving into features.
- Breakthrough with Lu Chuan:
  - Kekexili: Mountain Patrol (2004): Rugged, natural‑light location work on the Tibetan Plateau; wide‑angle landscapes and a semi‑documentary approach that helped define 2000s “new realist” Chinese cinema.
  - City of Life and Death (2009): Monumental black‑and‑white imagery of the Nanjing Massacre; tightly choreographed handheld work and stark chiaroscuro. This film cemented his reputation internationally.
  - The Last Supper (2012): Controlled palette, sculptural lighting, and period textures in a historical epic.
  - Chronicles of the Ghostly Tribe (2015): Large‑format spectacle photography, extensive VFX integration.
- Work with Guan Hu:
  - The Eight Hundred (2020): Immersive battlefield cinematography in IMAX/large format; dense atmospherics (smoke, debris, searchlights), sweeping crane work, and complex night exteriors. One of China’s biggest box‑office hits and a calling card for contemporary Chinese large‑scale cinematography.
- Other mainstream hits:
  - Crazy Alien (2019, dir. Ning Hao): High‑energy, precision camera movement for physical comedy and VFX.
- Visual trademarks:
  - Willingness to push format/technology (large‑format, IMAX, complex continuous takes).
  - Strong control of atmosphere (fog, smoke, dust) and high‑contrast lighting to model space and scale.
  - A blend of kinetic handheld work with classic, carefully composed wides.

Selected filmography (cinematographer)
- Kekexili: Mountain Patrol (2004, dir. Lu Chuan)
- City of Life and Death (a.k.a. Nanjing! Nanjing!, 2009, dir. Lu Chuan)
- The Last Supper (2012, dir. Lu Chuan)
- Chronicles of the Ghostly Tribe (2015, dir. Lu Chuan)
- Crazy Alien (2019, dir. Ning Hao)
- The Eight Hundred (2020, dir. Guan Hu)

Awards and recognition
- Multiple major Chinese‑language industry prizes for cinematography, including wins/nominations at:
  - Golden Horse Awards (Taiwan) — widely cited for Kekexili and City of Life and Death.
  - Asian Film Awards — recognition for City of Life and Death.
  - Mainland awards such as Golden Rooster and Hundred Flowers, with The Eight Hundred earning broad craft recognition.
- City of Life and Death won the Golden Shell at San Sebastián (2009); Cao Yu’s cinematography was frequently singled out by critics and juries even when an award was not specifically his.

Personal
- Married to actress Yao Chen (married 2012); they have two children.
- Not to be confused with the renowned 20th‑century Chinese playwright Cao Yu (a different person).

If you want, I can list specific award years and citations film by film, or detail the cameras/lenses and lighting strategies he used on titles like The Eight Hundred and City of Life and Death.
